name: maps every pixel into rectangular patches with the requested axis order
preserves patch raster order independently from channel order
input: position-encoded pixels split into multiple patch rows and columns
test:
import numpy as np
image = np.empty((4, 6, 2), dtype=np.int32)
for row in range(4):
    for col in range(6):
        for channel in range(2):
            image[row, col, channel] = 100 * row + 10 * col + channel
result = patchify_channels_first(image, 2, 2)
assert result.shape == (2, 3, 2, 2, 2)
assert np.array_equal(result[0, 1, 0], np.array([[20, 30], [120, 130]]))
assert np.array_equal(result[1, 2, 1], np.array([[241, 251], [341, 351]]))
assert np.array_equal(result[:, :, 1, 0, 0], np.array([[1, 21, 41], [201, 221, 241]]))

name: handles whole-image and unit patches on a non-contiguous image view
input: a strided 3-by-4 two-channel view with boundary patch sizes
test:
import numpy as np
base = np.arange(6 * 8 * 2, dtype=np.int16).reshape(6, 8, 2)
image = base[::2, ::2, :]
assert not image.flags.c_contiguous
whole = patchify_channels_first(image, 3, 4)
assert whole.shape == (1, 1, 2, 3, 4)
assert np.array_equal(whole[0, 0, 0], image[:, :, 0])
assert np.array_equal(whole[0, 0, 1], image[:, :, 1])
unit = patchify_channels_first(image, 1, 1)
assert unit.shape == (3, 4, 2, 1, 1)
assert np.array_equal(unit[:, :, :, 0, 0], image)
